text:
maya: heads-up — ap3a pool-6 (rack19) showing sustained correctable ECC uptick. two nodes flapping kernels and a few short panics. can we drain and move non-urgent workloads out?
chris: which nodes?
maya: ap3a-rk19-n23, ap3a-rk19-n24, ap3a-rk19-n27. metrics: ECC correctable rate went 120/hr -> ~900/hr over last 45m, UCEs 2 -> 6 in 30m.
sandeep: yikes. any network loss too or just GPU errors?
maya: mostly GPU errors, but we saw packet retransmits on the node NICs coincidentally for n24. not sure if related. attaching recent dmesg snippet: ```[ 23456.789] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, 13 00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000```
lia: we should drain those hosts ASAP. we have spare capacity in us-east dedicated (2 gpus) but shifting everything cross-region will add egress cost. prefer to route only low-priority batch jobs to eu-west and use us-east for interactive if needed.
rafa: current pool utilization: ap3a pool6 at 92% for realtime, batch burst at 78%. eu-west spare nodes can take ~30% of batch q, us-east dedicated has 2 GPUs free for latency-sensitive.
chris: plan: 1) cordon & drain the three nodes 2) shift batch jobs to eu-west queue with rate limit 3) route critical realtime to us-east dedicated (limit concurrency) 4) monitor error rate and vendor RMA if UCEs persist.
oncall-infra: alert created INC-4721 for ap3a-rk19 ECC surge. vendor contact: vendor-gpu-support.
maya: executing drain now. using: ```kubectl cordon ap3a-rk19-n23 && kubectl drain ap3a-rk19-n23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data```
chris: add in-flight cache flush for models on those nodes to avoid stale KV cache: ```/opt/runtime/bin/kvcache flush --node ap3a-rk19-n23```
sandeep: for traffic shift, use routing policy: ```route-policy set --from ap3a --to eu-west --tag batch --max-egress-gbps 1.5``` — keeps egress cost bounded.
lia: also enable soft-fallback smaller quantized model for realtime requests that can't be routed, reduces GPU memory pressure: set model_fallback=quantized-70 on ap3a pool config.
rafa: note: switching to quantized model will increase latency slightly (~5-12ms) but reduces mem by ~40% and may avoid queue spikes.
chris: drain started for n23 and n24. n27 shows short kernel panic during cordon; moving to immediate isolate.
devops-bot: [automated] cordon completed: ap3a-rk19-n23, ap3a-rk19-n24. Pods evacuated: 34, 29 respectively.
maya: good. starting traffic-shift now, throttling batch to eu-west 1.0 Gbps for first 15m then scale.
sandeep: tracking cost impact — estimated cross-region egress at $0.08/GB; with current batch reroute we expect ~$120/hr increase if sustained. will update finance if >4hr.
chris: hardware logs show increasing ECC correctables on n27 too; filing hardware RMA and requesting vendor pre-authorization for next-day swap.
oncall-infra: INC-4721 updated: vendor dispatched, ETA on-site 18-24h.
maya: after drain completion, performance dashboards show 10% tail-latency bump for some realtime routes during reroute window. lia, can you validate if SLAs affected?
lia: checking. realtime SLO still 99.5% for top-tier; mid-tier SLO dipped to 98.6% for 12m window. we should notify customers on dedicated contracts if this extends.
rafa: continuing capacity watch. if eu-west warms up and us-east dedicated is still low, we can migrate additional batch to eu-west to relieve ap3a.
chris: aggregating pod logs from evacuated nodes for postmortem: ```tar -czf evac-logs-ap3a-rk19.tgz /var/log/pods/*ap3a-rk19*```
maya: RMA ticket INC-4721 includes logs and vendor has serials. putting nodes into maintenance state and marking for hot-swap.
devops-bot: maintenance window scheduled: ap3a-rk19 22:00-02:00 UTC, replacement mode hot-swap.
sandeep: optional cost mitigator: we can temporarily reduce batch training preempts and bump priority for critical prod to keep errors from cascading. agree?
lia: yes, do that. chris please implement preempt policy: set batch_preempt=true for ap3a-pool6.
chris: done. batch preempt enabled. will monitor for queue thrash.
maya: final check — all three nodes drained and isolated. monitoring for 2h. will update here and open postmortem if vendor confirms HW fault after RMA. :thumbsup:
